scope: Received TimingData plus strictly earlier recorded SessionStatus, TrackStatus and sparse TimingAppData. No final lap CSV, IsAccurate, model fitting or new downloads.

observed_packet_structure_only.example: 202301 driver1 counter1->2 at packet4346 has LastLapTime1:37.974 but noS3; packet4347 supplies S3=24.128 at a31ms later recorded clock. This is preserved as a later diagnostic update, not a retroactive upgrade. Normal new S1 packets clear old S2/S3 display slots.

packet_clock: Reuse immutable sector_pilot.ledger.records metadata. available_ms is cumulative maximum recorded clock in each physical stream, not historical client receipt. Never backdate a malformed payload whose timestamp can be parsed. Aux records are consumed only when available_ms < current TimingData available_ms; equal timestamps are unavailable. No arbitrary auxiliary-file truncation or cross-stream network-receipt guarantee is claimed.
association: Save the old observed epoch before a counter change. An eligible completion requires an exact integer unit increment, unambiguous ordered S1 and S2 received in earlier packets of that old epoch, and positive S3 plus LastLapTime in the same counter-advance packet. S1/S2 values in the closing packet cannot repair missing prior sectors. All counter boundaries, including initialization/jump/reversal, and positive unassigned S3/LastLapTime updates emit immutable records with explicit reasons.
epochs: Observed counters are not certified canonical LapNumber. Initialize a fresh epoch on every valid counter change; jumps and reversed/quarantined epochs are ambiguous. After reversal, quarantine persists until the counter exceeds its previous highwater. S1/S2 at or within5000ms after a boundary are ambiguous. A changed positive sector value or a clear after an observed positive sector marks the epoch ambiguous; unchanged repeats retain the first available positive source. Ordinary clears of already-empty new-epoch S2/S3 slots are harmless. No later update repairs a previously emitted completion.
late_and_revised_completion_updates: Positive S3/LastLapTime without a counter advance is emitted separately. When it follows the latest boundary by at most5000ms with unchanged counter, it may reference that immutable completion and retain its earlier fields for a diagnostic sum check; its association is explicitly ambiguous and it never becomes eligible history. Otherwise it remains unassigned. Old completion records are never changed or removed.
quality_proxy: Eligible history additionally requires positive finite S1/S2/S3 and LastLapTime; known Started and TrackStatus1or2 throughout the observed epoch; known InPit=False throughout; no observed PitOut=True, retirement/stoppage or TrackStatus4/5/6/7 during the epoch; no parsing, timestamp or counter-attribution ambiguity. Observe every received control transition before each global TimingData packet, including transitions between two driver updates. This raw clean proxy does not assert final IsAccurate, physical lap validity or original receipt availability.

equation.interpretation: A fixed millisecond-display coherence check allowing rounding/truncation of component times; not an accuracy certificate or a selected prediction parameter.

tyres: Carry only sparse TimingAppData values already received strictly before the TimingData packet, recording highest observed stint index, source clock/sequence and candidate compound transitions. This is support metadata only; it does not certify an active stint or canonical TyreLife and does not supply invented tyre age.
consumer: Use only observed_valid_completed records with available_ms strictly less than the forecast checkpoint. Issue all forecasts at a shared timestamp before admitting any completion at that timestamp; peer histories obey the same clock. Diagnostic revisions never replace a prior training/history row.
api: iter_packets(path, stats=None) wraps the immutable pilot parser. iter_completed(paths, event_key, stats=None) yields JSON-serializable completion records. paths requires TimingData, SessionStatus, TrackStatus and TimingAppData. Optional stats is a mutable dictionary populated with counts. No file writes occur inside either iterator.
limits: Only two discovery races were inspected for message structure. No predictive scores were computed. Other sessions can legitimately yield fewer eligible records; missing/ambiguous data remain explicit rather than being repaired with final CSVs.
